findings.issue: Custom in-memory TTL/LRU cache reimplements the framework's fetch revalidate / use cache + cacheLife semantics on top of cache: 'no-store'
findings.suggestion: Either use fetch(url, { next: { revalidate: 30 } }) or the stable cacheLife API, or keep the bespoke cache but document in code why the built-in options were rejected (e.g. in-flight promise dedupe across requests)

findings.issue: All routes are dynamic (connection() in app/src/lib/api.ts:40) and every Link has prefetch={false}, so cold navigation to /pokemon/:name blocks on 100+ API fetches with no loading UI — the exact slow-transition pattern the docs warn about
findings.suggestion: Add loading.tsx skeletons for the dynamic detail routes and drop the now-redundant prefetch={false} (prefetch is skipped for dynamic routes anyway)

findings.issue: API responses flow through the app as any (api<T = any>, casts in page.tsx), so strict TypeScript verifies almost nothing at the data boundary
findings.suggestion: Define response types for the handful of resources actually used (species, pokemon, move, ability, type, generation) and type api<T> at call sites

findings.issue: The game <select> is controlled by useSearchParams whose only update path is history.replaceState; correctness rests on Next's patched history API re-syncing hooks, and popstate entries with null state hard-reload
findings.suggestion: Mirror the selection in useState (initialised from searchParams) and write the URL alongside it, or add a comment pinning the sync contract

findings.issue: Four detail pages duplicate the same lowercase-name/apiOrNull/notFound/generateMetadata boilerplate
findings.suggestion: Extract a small loadResource(resource, name) helper or per-resource factory in lib/api.ts

findings.issue: apiBase is prop-drilled through page → PokemonCardList → PokemonCard / HomeView, spreading environment plumbing through the component tree
findings.suggestion: Provide it via a context module or a client-side env (e.g. expose a getApiBase() in a shared module initialised once on the server)

findings.issue: An out-of-range ?page=999 renders the last page but leaves page=999 in the URL, so Previous page links to 998 and history is inconsistent
findings.suggestion: Replace the URL with the clamped page (or omit page) when filters.page exceeds pageCount

findings.issue: Row key ${move}-${level}-${rows.length} is a fragile synthetic key (can collide when the same move appears at the same level in different positions)
findings.suggestion: Key by the composite of move, level and method, or make the row data carry a stable unique id

findings.issue: Hand-written Props = { params: Promise<...> } in every page instead of Next 16's generated PageProps<'/pokemon/[name]'> from next typegen
findings.suggestion: Run next typegen and use the generated PageProps helpers for full type safety on route params

findings.issue: latestEnglishFlavorText also accepts a text field variant that no used API response has — speculative generality in a shared helper
findings.suggestion: Drop the unused text fallback until a caller actually needs it

summary: A clean, compact App Router codebase that is clearly aligned with current Next 16 practice (async params, generateMetadata/viewport exports, the documented native-history-API pattern for URL-driven filtering, Turbopack config) and has a small, well-bounded lib layer. The main review asks are a bespoke TTL cache where the framework has caching primitives, no loading/error UI on heavy all-dynamic routes, and pervasive any at the API boundary. I'd merge after one round of minor changes.
